name: RTC-001 - Mediasoup SFU Worker Initialization
Description:
Set up the core Mediasoup C++ worker processes wrapped in a Node.js API. Expectation: Media workers can successfully spawn and listen for WebRTC transports.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Node.js service running `mediasoup` installed
- Dynamic port allocation for WebRTC UDP/TCP traffic (e.g., 40000-49999) configured
- Worker processes scale based on CPU cores available in the container
- API endpoint to health-check worker load

name: RTC-002 - WebRTC Transport & Signaling Integration
Description:
Integrate the SFU with the existing Socket.io signaling layer built by Kay. Expectation: Clients can successfully exchange SDP offers/answers.

Acceptance Criteria:
- WebSocket event handlers for `createWebRtcTransport`, `connectWebRtcTransport`, `produce`, and `consume`
- Secure DTLS fingerprint exchange between client and SFU
- Implementation of Producer (sending media) and Consumer (receiving media) logic
- Handles WebRTC connection state changes (connecting, connected, disconnected)

name: RTC-003 - Global Coturn (TURN/STUN) Deployment
Description:
Deploy and configure Coturn servers in India, South America, and North America. Expectation: Clients behind strict firewalls can relay media.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Coturn installed on isolated VMs in Mumbai, São Paulo, and N. Virginia
- Configured with ephemeral short-term credentials via REST API secret
- Supports both UDP and TCP relaying (TLS port 443 fallback)
- SFU returns the optimal TURN server array based on the client's geolocation

name: RTC-004 - Simulcast Configuration & Publisher Logic
Description:
Configure Mediasoup to accept Simulcast streams from publishers (multiple video qualities). Expectation: A single publisher sends 3 spatial layers.

Acceptance Criteria:
- SFU accepts `low`, `medium`, and `high` spatial layers from a single video track
- Temporal layers (fps scaling) enabled
- Codec preference order configured (VP8, H.264, VP9)
- Logs verify that the server is receiving multiple bitrates for the same track

name: RTC-005 - Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) & Consumer Routing
Description:
Implement dynamic consumer routing to switch spatial layers based on consumer network conditions. Expectation: Consumers on bad networks get lower quality video instead of freezing.

Acceptance Criteria:
- SFU monitors consumer RTCP Receiver Reports for packet loss and jitter
- Automatically drops the consumer to the `low` spatial layer if packet loss > 5%
- Automatically upgrades to `high` spatial layer when network stabilizes
- Implements active speaker detection to give high resolution only to the speaker

name: RTC-006 - Audio-First Fallback Mechanism
Description:
Implement strict audio-first fallback logic for severe network degradation. Expectation: Audio never drops even if video fails completely.

Acceptance Criteria:
- If packet loss exceeds critical threshold (e.g., >15%), SFU temporarily pauses forwarding all video tracks to that consumer
- Audio track forwarding remains prioritized and uninterrupted
- Emits WebSocket event `video_paused_network` to the client so UI can show a 'Poor Network' avatar
- Auto-resumes video forwarding when RTCP reports improve

name: RTC-007 - SFU Horizontal Scaling & Router Piping
Description:
Implement router piping to allow meetings to span multiple SFU worker processes or distinct servers. Expectation: A room can hold 1,000+ people by distributing load.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Logic to detect when a single Mediasoup router hits capacity (~500 consumers)
- Automatically spawns a secondary router on a different worker/node
- Establishes `PipeTransport` between the two routers to share Producer tracks
- Clients seamlessly consume tracks regardless of which specific worker they connected to

name: RTC-008 - Media Recording Endpoint & GStreamer Integration
Description:
Implement raw media extraction from the SFU to pipe into a recording microservice. Expectation: Server-side recording of video/audio.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Consumes Producer tracks server-side using PlainTransport
- Pipes RTP packets into GStreamer or FFmpeg processes
- Mixes audio and video tracks into a unified MP4 or WebM file
- Uploads final recording file to Digital Ocean Spaces upon meeting end
